question.knowledge_point: Calculating the Times at Which a Particle Is Stationary
question.problem:
A particle $P$ moves in the $x$-$y$ plane (relative to a fixed origin $O$) with position vector

$$
r=⟨{t}^{3}-3t,{t}^{3}-6{t}^{2}+9t⟩,\,t\in [0,\infty ).
$$

Calculate the times at which the particle is stationary.
question.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the velocity vector $v.$ Differentiating the position vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3}-3t),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3}-6{t}^{2}+9t)⟩ \\  & =⟨3{t}^{2}-3,3{t}^{2}-12t+9⟩ \\  & =⟨3({t}^{2}-1),3({t}^{2}-4t+3)⟩ \\  & =⟨3(t+1)(t-1),3(t-1)(t-3)⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

The particle is stationary when its velocity is zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =0 \\ ⟨3(t+1)(t-1),3(t-1)(t-3)⟩ & =⟨0,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

So we need

$$
\begin{aligned}3(t+1)(t-1)=0\, & ⇒\,t=\pm 1, \\ 3(t-1)(t-3)=0\, & ⇒\,t=1,3.\end{aligned}
$$

The solution $t=1$ is the only solution that satisfies both equations, so this is the only value of $t$ when the particle is stationary.
